sections.title: What to Use, and When
sections.summary: Practical starting points for sleep, focus, anxiety, meditation, training, and recovery.

articles.title: For sleep
articles.body:
**Start with:** Delta or Theta in the Generator.

Theta if you want to drift down gradually. Delta if you want to drop straight toward deep rest.

**Build the session.** Start the frequency, keep the volume low, and overlay a soft sound like rain or a fireplace so a pure tone is not the last thing your brain is tracking. Many people run 30 to 60 minutes rather than the whole night.

**Add the breathing exercise** for the first minute to slow your breath before the frequency does its work.

**If your mind is racing,** generate an AI meditation about whatever is keeping you up and let it run first, then move to a delta session.

**A note on wearing them all night.** The battery gives you about 6 hours and the pads press against your face. Most people find a timed session before sleep more comfortable than sleeping in them.

articles.title: For focus and deep work
articles.body:
**Start with:** Alpha in the Generator.

Alpha is calm alertness, which is what sustained work actually needs. Beta suits active problem solving and conversation. Gamma is for heavy cognitive load and it makes some people jittery, so try alpha before you reach for it.

**Build the session.** Alpha frequency, brown or white noise or a low ambient sound over the top, earplugs in if the room is noisy.

**Program a quick action button** with your focus frequency so a single press starts your session without unlocking your phone.

**Session length.** Work in blocks of 45 to 90 minutes. Reset between blocks rather than running the same tone for six hours straight.

articles.title: For anxiety and stress
articles.body:
**Start with:** Alpha, or the Calm Focus entry in the Frequency Library.

Alpha slows things down without putting you to sleep, which is usually what you want in the middle of a day that has gotten away from you.

**Build the session.** Frequency first, then the breathing exercise, then a nature sound layered underneath. Ten minutes is enough to change something.

**Read Your Frequency** is useful here, because when you are anxious you often cannot name what you need. Say the affirmation, take the recommendation, and start.

**If the anxiety is about something specific,** generate an AI meditation naming that thing directly. Specific beats general.

If you are dealing with anxiety that interferes with your daily life, work with a clinician. This is a tool alongside care, not a replacement for it.

articles.title: For meditation
articles.body:
**If you already have a practice:** run theta in the Generator underneath your usual sitting. Sync a Solfeggio tone if you prefer a single pure frequency to two.

**If you are new to it:** use the AI meditation generator. Speak what is on your mind and let it guide you rather than sitting in silence trying to do it correctly.

**For a deeper session:** the Gateway Experience entries in the Frequency Library work through progressive levels and are worth exploring once you are comfortable with theta.

**After the session,** generate affirmations from the meditation and loop them through the day.

articles.title: For training, energy, and recovery
articles.body:
**Before training:** Beta or Gamma for activation, with the headphones on and your ears open so you can hear the room and stay aware of your surroundings.

**During training:** the headphones work as normal Bluetooth headphones, so play your music. Your ears stay open, which matters if you are running outside.

**After training:** Alpha or Theta to come down, or Delta for a recovery nap.

**For soreness and rest,** low delta with a long sound bed. Keep the volume low and let the session run while you lie still.

articles.title: For attention and restlessness
articles.body:
J built the product around his own experience with ADHD and Vyvanse, so this is the use case the company knows best.

**Start with:** Alpha for calm focus. If alpha feels too soft, try beta.

**Try the modulating option.** Tap the brain icon so the frequencies move rather than hold steady. Many people who find a constant tone boring or easy to tune out respond better to movement.

**Program a quick action button** so starting a session takes one press instead of a chain of decisions that gives you an opportunity to get distracted.

**Consistency matters more than intensity.** Same time, same setup, every day.

This is a wellness tool. It is not a treatment for ADHD and it does not replace medication or medical advice. Do not change a prescription without talking to your prescriber.

articles.title: How often and how long
articles.body:
**Session length.** Ten minutes is the floor for anything to register. Twenty to forty-five minutes is the range most people settle into. Focus blocks can run longer.

**Frequency of use.** Daily beats intense. A short session every day does more than a two-hour session once a week.

**Building the habit.** Attach it to something you already do. First coffee, start of a work block, lights out. Use the Sound Setting reminder to prompt you.

**Can you overdo it.** Long sessions at high volume are hard on your hearing and can leave your face feeling numb. If you feel headachy, wired, or uncomfortable, stop and lower the volume next time. More is not better.

faqs.q: What should I use for studying?
faqs.a: Alpha with a low ambient sound over it, in 45 to 90 minute blocks. Beta if the material demands active problem solving rather than absorption.

faqs.q: What should I use before a presentation or interview?
faqs.a: Alpha for ten minutes to settle, or an AI meditation naming the specific event. Save gamma for after, since it can add to the buzz rather than calm it.

faqs.q: Can I use it at work with people around?
faqs.a: Yes. Bone conduction leaves your ears open so you can hear someone speaking to you. Keep the volume moderate, since there is some audible leakage at high volume.

faqs.q: Can I listen while reading or writing?
faqs.a: Yes. Pure tones distract some people while they read. Overlay a sound, or use a Solfeggio tone with both ears synced, which many people find easier to ignore.

faqs.q: How long before I see real results?
faqs.a: The in-session effect is usually immediate. Lasting change comes from repetition, so give it two to four weeks of daily use before you judge it.

faqs.q: Can I use it more than once a day?
faqs.a: Yes. A common pattern is focus in the morning, a reset in the afternoon, and delta before sleep. Watch your volume across the day.

faqs.q: Does it work for tinnitus?
faqs.a: Some people with tinnitus find sound and frequency masking helpful and some find it makes things worse. Start at very low volume and stop if it aggravates the ringing. Speak to an audiologist about tinnitus specifically.

faqs.q: Can I use it for pain?
faqs.a: People use low frequency sessions for relaxation while dealing with discomfort. The app does not treat pain and is not a medical device. See a doctor about pain that persists.

sections.title: Troubleshooting
sections.summary: Fixes for the problems people actually run into.

articles.title: I cannot feel any vibration
articles.body:
Work through these in order.

1. **Check what you are playing.** Sounds do not vibrate the transducers on their own. Open the Generator and start an actual frequency.
2. **Check placement.** The pads must sit on your cheekbones, on bone, just in front of your ears. On the ear or on soft tissue kills the vibration.
3. **Check contact.** Thick hair, a hat, or glasses arms between the pad and your skin dampen it.
4. **Raise the volume slowly.** Vibration intensity scales with volume.
5. **Try a lower frequency.** Low frequencies vibrate far more noticeably than high ones. If you were on a 528 Hz tone, try delta or theta and compare.
6. **Confirm the audio is routing to the headphones,** not your phone speaker. Check the output selector on the player screen.

articles.title: The headphones will not pair
articles.body:
1. Confirm the headphones are charged. Low battery causes intermittent pairing failures.
2. Power them on and hold the power button until the indicator shows pairing mode.
3. Open Bluetooth in your phone settings, not the app. Pairing happens at the system level.
4. If the headphones appear as connected but produce no sound, tap forget this device in your Bluetooth settings and pair again from scratch.
5. Turn Bluetooth off and back on, or restart your phone.
6. Disconnect them from any other device. They connect to one source at a time.

Still stuck: contact support with your phone model, OS version, and what you see in your Bluetooth list.

articles.title: No sound at all
articles.body:
1. Check your phone is not muted and the media volume is up. Ringer volume and media volume are separate.
2. Check the output routing on the player screen and select the headphones.
3. If a sound will not stream, check your connection. Frequencies work offline, sounds do not unless downloaded.
4. Force close the app and reopen it.
5. Confirm the app has permission to play audio and is not being throttled by battery saver mode.
6. If only one ear plays on a Solfeggio tone, that is the sync button rather than a fault. Tap the middle button to sync both ears.

articles.title: App crashes, slow screens, and stuck loading
articles.body:
**Leaderboard stuck loading.** Known issue and being fixed. Close it and try again shortly.

**Reminders not firing.** Sound Setting has a known bug. Confirm notifications are enabled for the app in your phone settings while it is being fixed.

**Read Your Frequency not responding.** Check microphone permission for the app. This feature has also been unstable in test builds.

**General crashes.** Force close and reopen, then check the App Store or Google Play for an update. If it persists, delete and reinstall, then use restore purchase to bring your premium back.

**Distorted audio when mixing.** Pull individual layer volumes down or remove layers. There is no hard limit on how many sounds you can stack, and large stacks have not been fully tested.

When you contact support, include your phone model, OS version, app version, and what you were doing when it happened. That combination is what lets the engineering team reproduce it.

faqs.q: I feel the vibration in one ear only.
faqs.a: On the Solfeggio tab, tap the middle sync button so both ears play the same tone. In the Generator, check that both the left and right sliders are above zero, since they are independent. If it persists across every tab, contact support because it may be a hardware fault.

faqs.q: The volume sliders are hard to grab.
faqs.a: Known issue with the current controls, particularly on smaller screens. Improved controls are part of the redesign.

faqs.q: I lost my streak and I did listen.
faqs.a: A streak day counts when you open the app and play something. Very short plays or a session that did not sync can miss. Contact support with the date and we will look at it.

faqs.q: My favorites or downloads disappeared.
faqs.a: Confirm you are signed in to the right account. Reinstalling clears downloads and you will need to save them again. Favorites are tied to your account, so if those are gone, contact support.

faqs.q: The app is draining my battery.
faqs.a: Real-time frequency generation with the screen on uses more power than streaming audio. Lock your screen during sessions, close the app when you are done, and download rather than stream where you can.

faqs.q: How do I update the app?
faqs.a: Through the App Store or Google Play like any other app. Turn on automatic updates so you get bug fixes as they ship.

faqs.q: One side of my headphones stopped working.
faqs.a: Unpair and repair first, and try them with a different device to isolate whether the issue is the headphones or the phone. If one transducer stays silent, contact support with your order number.

sections.title: Safety and Who Should Be Careful
sections.summary: Read this before your first session, particularly if you have a seizure disorder or a medical condition.

articles.title: Using it safely
articles.body:
High Frequency Highway is a wellness product. It does not diagnose, treat, cure, or prevent any disease, and it is not a medical device.

**Talk to your doctor first if any of these apply to you.**

- Epilepsy or any seizure disorder, or a history of seizures in your family. Rhythmic audio stimulation can be a trigger for some people.
- A pacemaker, cochlear implant, or any implanted electronic device.
- Pregnancy.
- A diagnosed psychiatric condition, or if you are currently in treatment.
- Hearing loss, tinnitus, or you wear hearing aids.

**Never use it while driving, cycling, or operating machinery.** Focus, sleep, and relaxation states are not compatible with anything that needs your full attention.

**Protect your hearing.** Volume is how you control vibration intensity, which creates pressure to turn it up. Long sessions at high volume damage hearing regardless of how the sound is delivered. Set it just high enough to feel a light buzz.

**Stop if you feel unwell.** Headache, dizziness, nausea, agitation, or visual disturbance means stop the session. If it happens again, stop using the product and speak to a doctor.

**Do not use it in place of medical care.** If you are managing a condition, keep working with your clinician. Do not change or stop a prescription because of anything you experience with this product.

articles.title: About the condition names in the Frequency Library
articles.body:
The Frequency Library contains entries named after specific health conditions. That naming comes from the historical Royal Rife research catalog, which is where a large portion of these frequency pairs originate.

Those names describe the category the frequency was filed under in that original research. They are not claims about what the frequency does, and they are not treatments.

The app does not diagnose, treat, cure, or prevent any disease. Nothing in the Frequency Library is a substitute for medical care, and no one should delay seeing a doctor because of it.

Use the library as a starting point for a listening session. Manage your health with a clinician.

faqs.q: Is it safe if I have epilepsy?
faqs.a: Talk to your doctor before using it. Rhythmic audio stimulation can be a seizure trigger for some people and we cannot assess your individual risk.

faqs.q: Is it safe during pregnancy?
faqs.a: There is no evidence of harm from listening to audio at moderate volume, and we are not in a position to give medical advice. Check with your doctor or midwife.

faqs.q: Can it damage my hearing?
faqs.a: Any audio at high volume for long periods can. Bone conduction is no exception. Keep the volume just high enough to feel a light buzz on your cheekbones and take breaks.

faqs.q: Can it cure or treat a medical condition?
faqs.a: No. This is a wellness product and not a medical device. It does not diagnose, treat, cure, or prevent any disease. The condition names in the Frequency Library come from a historical research catalog and are not treatment claims.

faqs.q: Why do I get a headache after using it?
faqs.a: Usually volume that is too high, a session that ran too long, or a frequency that does not suit you. Lower the volume, shorten the session, and try a different state. If headaches continue, stop and speak to a doctor.

faqs.q: Can I use it with my medication?
faqs.a: Listening to audio does not interact with medication. Do not change or stop any prescription because of anything you experience with this product. Talk to your prescriber about your treatment.

faqs.q: Is it safe for children?
faqs.a: Keep the volume low and supervise use. Do not use it with a child who has a seizure disorder without their doctor's guidance.

sections.title: Glossary
sections.summary: Plain-language definitions for every term the app uses.

articles.title: Terms you will see in the app
articles.body:
**Sound.** An audio file, streamed or downloaded. Rain, a fireplace, a sound bath, ambient music.

**Frequency.** A tone measured in hertz, generated live on your device. This is what vibrates the headphones.

**Hertz (Hz).** Cycles per second. 100 Hz means 100 vibrations per second.

**Bone conduction.** Sound delivered as vibration through the bones of your skull to your inner ear, bypassing the eardrum.

**Transducer.** The part of the headphone that rests on your cheekbone and vibrates.

**Binaural beats.** Two slightly different tones, one per ear. Your brain perceives a third tone at the difference between them.

**Frequency following effect.** Your brainwaves shifting to match the difference between the two tones you are hearing.

**Entrainment.** The process of your brain synchronizing to an external rhythm.

**Brainwave state.** The speed your neurons are firing at, grouped into named ranges: delta, theta, alpha, beta, gamma.

**Delta.** Roughly 0.5 to 4 Hz. Deep sleep and recovery.

**Theta.** Roughly 4 to 8 Hz. Drowsiness, deep meditation, creative drift.

**Alpha.** Roughly 8 to 12 Hz. Calm alertness.

**Beta.** Roughly 12 to 30 Hz. Active thinking.

**Gamma.** Roughly 30 to 100 Hz. Peak cognition and flow.

**Solfeggio.** A set of nine tones from historical sound healing traditions, including 528 Hz.

**Pure tone.** One frequency playing in both ears at the same value, rather than two different tones.

**Rife library.** A catalog of frequency pairs drawn from Royal Rife's research, organized by category name.

**Gateway Experience.** A structured series of frequency levels included in the Frequency Library.

**Mixer.** The control for layering multiple sounds with individual volume.

**Overlay.** Playing a sound on top of a running frequency, or a frequency under a sound.

**Modulation.** Frequencies moving up and down instead of holding steady. Toggled with the brain icon.

**Septa Sync.** A separately purchased playlist of seven frequencies, $39, currently in a research study with MIT.

**Batch.** A production run of headphones arriving from the manufacturer. Orders are filled against batches in the order they were placed.

**Queue position.** Where your order sits in line against every other unshipped order, oldest first. It drives your ship date.

**In transit.** Your package is with the carrier. From this point the tracker shows live carrier data rather than an estimate.
